Statement II: The Young's modulus and shear modulus of a material are valid and physically meaningful for liquids and gases.

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: हुक का नियम सभी ठोस पदार्थों के लिए उनके अंतिम त्रोटन (भंजन) बिंदु तक सर्वत्र मान्य होता है।

कथन II: किसी पदार्थ का यंग प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक और दृढ़ता गुणांक द्रवों तथा गैसों के लिए मान्य और भौतिक रूप से सार्थक होते हैं।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hooke's law is an empirical relation valid strictly within the proportional limit. Young's modulus and shear modulus require a material to have a definite length and fixed shape.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The statement claiming universal validity for Hooke's law is incorrect because Hooke's law is valid only in the initial linear portion of the stress-strain curve, failing across the plastic and necking regions. The statement regarding elastic moduli is also incorrect because fluids (liquids and gases) do not possess a fixed shape or definite longitudinal length to resist tensile or static shear stresses; hence, only bulk modulus is applicable to fluids.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: Both statements are incorrect because Hooke's law fails beyond the proportional limit, and Young's and shear moduli are meaningful only for solids.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
हुक का नियम केवल समानुपाती सीमा के भीतर मान्य होता है। यंग मापांक और दृढ़ता गुणांक केवल ठोस पदार्थों के लिए परिभाषित हैं।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
हुक के नियम से संबंधित कथन असत्य है क्योंकि यह केवल समानुपाती सीमा तक ही लागू होता है, भंजन बिंदु तक नहीं। प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक से संबंधित कथन भी असत्य है क्योंकि द्रवों और गैसों की कोई निश्चित आकृति या लंबाई नहीं होती, अतः उनके लिए केवल आयतन मापांक परिभाषित होता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
दोनों कथन गलत हैं।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: दोनों कथन गलत हैं क्योंकि हुक का नियम समानुपाती सीमा के बाद मान्य नहीं होता, तथा यंग और दृढ़ता गुणांक केवल ठोसों के लिए अर्थपूर्ण हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q03 - Elastic comparison between steel and rubber

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In physical science, steel is considered more elastic than rubber because it has a significantly higher Young's modulus.

Statement II: A material that undergoes a large elongation under a small tensile load is considered more elastic in physics than one which stretches very little.

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: भौतिक विज्ञान में स्टील को रबर की तुलना में अधिक प्रत्यास्थ माना जाता है क्योंकि इसका यंग प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक काफी अधिक होता है।

कथन II: जो पदार्थ कम तनाव भार के अंतर्गत अधिक लंबाई में वृद्धि दर्शाता है, उसे भौतिकी में कम खिंचने वाले पदार्थ की तुलना में अधिक प्रत्यास्थ माना जाता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Modulus of elasticity is defined as stress per unit strain (\(Y = \sigma / \varepsilon\)). Elasticity measures resistance to deformation and restoring capacity rather than extensibility.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The statement affirming that steel is more elastic than rubber is correct because for a given strain, steel requires a vastly greater stress than rubber, yielding a much larger Young's modulus. The statement asserting that materials stretching more are scientifically more elastic is incorrect; everyday language confuses stretchability with elasticity, whereas in scientific terms, greater elasticity implies that a material resists deformation more strongly and exerts a greater restoring force.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first assertion regarding steel being more elastic is correct, while the second assertion equating large elongation with greater elasticity is incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: Steel is more elastic than rubber due to its higher Young's modulus, but materials that stretch more easily are less elastic in physics.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक प्रति एकांक विकृति के लिए आवश्यक प्रतिबल (\(Y = \sigma / \varepsilon\)) है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
स्टील के अधिक प्रत्यास्थ होने से संबंधित कथन सत्य है क्योंकि स्टील का यंग मापांक रबर से कहीं अधिक है। अधिक खिंचने वाले पदार्थ को अधिक प्रत्यास्थ मानने वाला कथन असत्य है; भौतिकी में जो पदार्थ दिए गए भार के लिए कम खिंचता है (विरूपण का अधिक विरोध करता है), वह अधिक प्रत्यास्थ होता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
स्टील के अधिक प्रत्यास्थ होने का विचार सही है, जबकि अधिक खिंचाव को अधिक प्रत्यास्थता मानना गलत है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: उच्च यंग मापांक के कारण स्टील रबर से अधिक प्रत्यास्थ है, लेकिन भौतिकी में आसानी से खिंचने वाले पदार्थ कम प्रत्यास्थ माने जाते हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q04 - Deformation of helical spring and bulk modulus applicability

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When a helical coil spring is stretched along its axis, the extension of the spring is determined predominantly by the Young's modulus of the wire material.

Statement II: Bulk modulus is relevant for all three states of matter—solids, liquids, and gases.

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जब किसी कुंडलिनी स्प्रिंग को उसके अक्ष के अनुदिश खींचा जाता है, तो स्प्रिंग का प्रसार मुख्य रूप से तार के पदार्थ के यंग मापांक द्वारा निर्धारित होता है।

कथन II: आयतन प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक पदार्थ की तीनों अवस्थाओं—ठोस, द्रव और गैस—के लिए प्रासंगिक और मान्य है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Axial elongation of a helical coil spring causes the coiled wire to twist, producing torsional shear strain across its cross-section. Bulk modulus quantifies volumetric response under uniform pressure.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The statement claiming that helical spring stretching is determined by Young's modulus is incorrect because axial extension twists the coiled wire, so the deformation is governed by the shear modulus (modulus of rigidity \(G\)). The statement stating that bulk modulus is relevant for solids, liquids, and gases is correct because all states of matter have volume and experience volume contraction under uniform hydraulic pressure.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The helical spring assertion is incorrect, whereas the bulk modulus applicability assertion is correct.

Final Conceptual Answer: The extension of a helical spring is governed by shear modulus rather than Young's modulus, and bulk modulus is indeed relevant for solids, liquids, and gases.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
कुंडलिनी स्प्रिंग के अक्षीय खिंचाव से तार में ऐंठन (मरोड़) उत्पन्न होती है, जो अपरूपण विरूपण है। आयतन मापांक एकसमान दाब में आयतन परिवर्तन से संबंधित है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
स्प्रिंग के खिंचाव को यंग मापांक द्वारा निर्धारित बताने वाला कथन असत्य है क्योंकि यह दृढ़ता (अपरूपण) गुणांक \(G\) पर निर्भर करता है। आयतन मापांक के तीनों अवस्थाओं के लिए प्रासंगिक होने से संबंधित कथन सत्य है क्योंकि सभी अवस्थाओं का आयतन दाब के साथ बदलता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
स्प्रिंग के खिंचाव का यंग मापांक पर निर्भर होना गलत है, जबकि आयतन मापांक का तीनों अवस्थाओं के लिए मान्य होना सही है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: कुंडलिनी स्प्रिंग का खिंचाव यंग मापांक के बजाय दृढ़ता गुणांक द्वारा निर्धारित होता है, तथा आयतन मापांक वास्तव में ठोस, द्रव और गैस तीनों के लिए प्रासंगिक है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q05 - Work done and energy density in wire stretching

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The work done in stretching a wire of original length \(L\) and cross-sectional area \(A\) by an elongation \(l\) is equal to \(\frac{1}{2} F l\), where \(F\) is the final applied tensile load.

Statement II: The elastic potential energy stored per unit volume of a stretched wire is equal to half the product of stress and strain.

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: मूल लंबाई \(L\) तथा अनुप्रस्थ-काट क्षेत्रफल \(A\) वाले तार को \(l\) प्रसार तक खींचने में किया गया कार्य \(\frac{1}{2} F l\) के बराबर होता है, जहाँ \(F\) अंतिम अनुप्रयुक्त तनाव भार है।

कथन II: किसी खिंचे हुए तार के प्रति एकांक आयतन में संचित प्रत्यास्थ स्थितिज ऊर्जा, प्रतिबल और विकृति के गुणनफल के आधे के बराबर होती है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
During stretching within Hooke's law, the restoring force varies linearly from \(0\) to \(F\), giving average force \(\frac{F}{2}\). Energy density is total energy divided by volume \(A L\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The statement regarding work done is correct because \(W = \int_0^l \frac{Y A x}{L} dx = \frac{Y A l^2}{2 L} = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{Y A l}{L}\right) l = \frac{1}{2} F l\). The statement regarding energy density is also correct because dividing total work \(W = \frac{1}{2} F l\) by volume \(V = A L\) yields \(u = \frac{W}{A L} = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{F}{A}\right) \left(\frac{l}{L}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \sigma \varepsilon\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are completely correct.

Final Conceptual Answer: Both statements are correct because the stretching work is half the product of final force and elongation, and the energy density is half the product of stress and strain.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
हुक के नियम के अंतर्गत प्रत्यानयन बल \(0\) से \(F\) तक रैखिक रूप से बढ़ता है, अतः औसत बल \(F/2\) होता है। ऊर्जा घनत्व कुल ऊर्जा बटे आयतन \(A L\) है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
कार्य से संबंधित कथन सही है क्योंकि \(W = \frac{1}{2} F l\) होता है। ऊर्जा घनत्व से संबंधित कथन भी सही है क्योंकि \(u = \frac{W}{A L} = \frac{1}{2} \sigma \varepsilon\) होता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
दोनों कथन पूर्णतः सही हैं।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: दोनों कथन सही हैं क्योंकि खींचने में किया गया कार्य अंतिम बल और प्रसार के गुणनफल का आधा है, तथा ऊर्जा घनत्व प्रतिबल और विकृति के गुणनफल का आधा है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q06 - Characteristics of ductile materials and permanent set

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a stress-strain graph, if the ultimate tensile strength point and the fracture point are very close to each other, the material is classified as ductile.

Statement II: When a material acquires a permanent set, it completely regains its original shape and dimensions once the deforming stress is removed.

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी प्रतिबल-विकृति आरेख में, यदि चरम तनन सामर्थ्य बिंदु और भंजन बिंदु एक-दूसरे के अत्यधिक निकट हों, तो पदार्थ को तन्य (डक्टाइल) के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है।

कथन II: जब कोई पदार्थ स्थायी विरूपण (परमानेंट सेट) प्राप्त कर लेता है, तो विरूपक प्रतिबल हटा लेने पर वह अपनी मूल आकृति और विमाओं को पूरी तरह पुनः प्राप्त कर लेता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ductility relates to a large plastic region between yield and fracture. Permanent set represents residual plastic strain when stress returns to zero.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The statement regarding ductile materials is incorrect because when the ultimate tensile strength and fracture points are close together, the material breaks with little plastic deformation and is called brittle, not ductile. The statement regarding permanent set is also incorrect because a permanent set means that even when stress is completely removed to zero, a residual strain remains and the material does not return to its original dimensions.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: Both statements are incorrect because closeness of ultimate strength and fracture points characterizes brittle materials, and a permanent set involves non-recoverable plastic strain.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
तन्यता पराभव बिंदु और भंजन बिंदु के बीच बड़े प्लास्टिक क्षेत्र से पहचानी जाती है। परमानेंट सेट प्रतिबल शून्य होने पर शेष बची विकृति है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
तन्य पदार्थ से संबंधित कथन असत्य है क्योंकि चरम सामर्थ्य और भंजन बिंदु निकट होने पर पदार्थ भंगुर कहलाता है, तन्य नहीं। परमानेंट सेट से संबंधित कथन भी असत्य है क्योंकि स्थायी विरूपण का अर्थ ही है कि प्रतिबल हटाने के बाद भी अवशिष्ट विकृति रह जाती है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
दोनों कथन गलत हैं।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: दोनों कथन गलत हैं क्योंकि चरम सामर्थ्य और भंजन बिंदु की निकटता भंगुर पदार्थों का लक्षण है, तथा स्थायी विरूपण में अप्रत्यास्थ अवशिष्ट विकृति रह जाती है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q07 - Sagittal depression of loaded beams and buckling

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: To minimize the central depression of a loaded beam of given length and material, increasing the depth \(d\) is far more effective than increasing the breadth \(b\).

Statement II: A deep and narrow rectangular beam can be made arbitrarily deep without any risk of sideways bending or buckling under load.

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: दिए गए पदार्थ और लंबाई की भारित बीम के केंद्रीय अवनमन को न्यूनतम करने के लिए, चौड़ाई \(b\) बढ़ाने की तुलना में गहराई \(d\) को बढ़ाना कहीं अधिक प्रभावी होता है।

कथन II: एक गहरी और संकीर्ण आयताकार बीम को भार के अंतर्गत बिना किसी पार्श्व मुड़ाव या बकलिंग के जोखिम के स्वेच्छिक रूप से गहरा बनाया जा सकता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Central depression of a rectangular beam is given by \(\delta = \frac{W L^3}{4 b d^3 Y}\). Structural stability requires preventing lateral-torsional buckling.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The statement concerning beam dimensions is correct because \(\delta\) is inversely proportional to the cube of depth (\(\delta \propto d^{-3}\)) and only inversely proportional to breadth (\(\delta \propto b^{-1}\)); thus, increasing depth produces a much sharper reduction in sagging. The statement concerning buckling is incorrect because increasing depth while keeping breadth small causes the bar to bend sideways and twist under vertical loads—a mechanical instability known as buckling.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The beam depression dependency on depth is correct, whereas the claim that deep beams never buckle is incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: Increasing beam depth is significantly more effective because depression scales as the inverse cube of depth, but excessively deep and narrow beams suffer from buckling instability.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
आयताकार बीम का अवनमन \(\delta = \frac{W L^3}{4 b d^3 Y}\) होता है। अत्यधिक गहराई से बीम में पार्श्व बकलिंग हो सकती है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
विमाओं से संबंधित कथन सत्य है क्योंकि अवनमन \(d^3\) के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है, अतः गहराई बढ़ाना अधिक प्रभावी है। बकलिंग न होने से संबंधित कथन असत्य है क्योंकि अत्यधिक पतली और गहरी पट्टी भार पड़ने पर एक तरफ मुड़ (बकल हो) जाती है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
गहराई बढ़ाने से अवनमन घटने की बात सही है, जबकि गहरी बीम में बकलिंग का जोखिम न होने का दावा गलत है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: बीम की गहराई बढ़ाना कहीं अधिक प्रभावी है क्योंकि अवनमन गहराई के घन के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है, परंतु अत्यधिक गहरी और संकीर्ण बीम बकलिंग अस्थिरता से ग्रस्त हो जाती है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q08 - Elastic limitation on mountain height and base stress nature

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The maximum theoretical height of mountains on Earth is limited to approximately 10 km because the bulk modulus of rock is exceeded at that depth.

Statement II: At the base of a high mountain, the lateral sides are unconfined, so the vertical gravitational force produces a shearing stress component rather than pure hydraulic compression.

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: पृथ्वी पर पर्वतों की अधिकतम सैद्धांतिक ऊँचाई लगभग 10 km तक सीमित है क्योंकि उस गहराई पर चट्टान का आयतन मापांक समाप्त हो जाता है।

कथन II: एक ऊँचे पर्वत के आधार पर, पार्श्व किनारे स्वतंत्र होते हैं, इसलिए ऊर्ध्वाधर गुरुत्वीय बल शुद्ध जलीय संपीडन के बजाय एक अपरूपण प्रतिबल घटक उत्पन्न करता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The height limit of mountains is determined by the critical shearing stress (elastic limit) of rock under unconfined vertical loading: \(h_{\text{max}} = \frac{\sigma_{\text{shear}}}{\rho g}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
The statement asserting that mountain height is limited by bulk modulus is incorrect because mountain failure is a shearing failure where rock flows laterally under vertical load, governed by the rock's shear elastic limit (\(\approx 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}\)), not bulk modulus. The statement explaining that the base is not under uniform hydrostatic compression because its lateral sides are free is correct, as this unconfined geometry directly generates the shearing stress \(\approx h \rho g\) responsible for plastic rock flow.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The bulk modulus limitation statement is incorrect, but the base shear stress statement is correct.

Final Conceptual Answer: Mountain height is limited by the rock's shear strength under lateral deformation rather than bulk modulus, and the unconfined base creates large shearing stresses.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत
पर्वत की अधिकतम ऊँचाई चट्टान की अपरूपण प्रत्यास्थ सीमा द्वारा \(h_{\text{max}} = \frac{\sigma_{\text{shear}}}{\rho g}\) से निर्धारित होती है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
आयतन मापांक द्वारा ऊँचाई सीमित होने से संबंधित कथन असत्य है क्योंकि पर्वत का आधार अपरूपण विफलता के कारण प्रवाहित होता है। आधार पर किनारे खुले होने से संबंधित कथन सत्य है क्योंकि पार्श्व स्वतंत्रता के कारण ही ऊर्ध्वाधर भार अपरूपण प्रतिबल उत्पन्न करता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
आयतन मापांक संबंधी कथन गलत है, जबकि आधार पर अपरूपण प्रतिबल से संबंधित कथन सही है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: पर्वत की ऊँचाई आयतन मापांक के बजाय पार्श्व विरूपण के तहत चट्टान की अपरूपण सामर्थ्य से सीमित होती है, तथा मुक्त आधार विशाल अपरूपण प्रतिबल उत्पन्न करता है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS11_CH08_STATEMENT3_Q01 - Applicability of elastic moduli to different states of matter

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the applicability of elastic moduli to different states of matter:

  1. Young's modulus and shear modulus are relevant only for solids because only solids have a definite shape.
  2. Bulk modulus is relevant for all three states of matter: solids, liquids, and gases.
  3. Gases are completely incompressible and possess an infinite bulk modulus under standard conditions.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

पदार्थ की विभिन्न अवस्थाओं के लिए प्रत्यास्थता गुणांकों की प्रासंगिकता के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

  1. यंग प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक और अपरूपण गुणांक केवल ठोसों के लिए प्रासंगिक हैं क्योंकि केवल ठोसों का ही एक निश्चित आकार होता है।
  2. आयतन प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक पदार्थ की तीनों अवस्थाओं: ठोस, द्रव और गैस के लिए प्रासंगिक है।
  3. गैसें पूरी तरह से असंपीड्य होती हैं और मानक परिस्थितियों में उनका आयतन प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक अनंत होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Elastic moduli describe how a medium responds to deforming forces. Solids possess a definite shape and volume, enabling them to sustain longitudinal tensile/compressive stresses (governed by Young's modulus \(Y\)) and shearing stresses (governed by shear modulus \(G\)). Fluids (liquids and gases) lack shear rigidity and cannot sustain static shearing stress without flowing.

Step 2: Analysis of Longitudinal and Shear Rigidity
Because fluids have no fixed shape and cannot resist tangential or shearing forces in static equilibrium, both Young's modulus and shear modulus are defined solely for solids. Therefore, the assertion that Young's modulus and shear modulus apply exclusively to solids is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Analysis of Volume Elasticity Across States
All three phases of matter—solids, liquids, and gases—undergo volume changes when subjected to uniform hydrostatic pressure. The bulk modulus \(B = -V \frac{\Delta P}{\Delta V}\) quantifies resistance to volumetric compression across all states of matter, making this assertion valid.

Step 4: Compressibility of Gases
Gases are highly compressible fluids whose volume decreases significantly under pressure. Compressibility \(k = \frac{1}{B}\) is exceptionally large for gases, meaning their bulk modulus \(B\) is finite and relatively small (for instance, isothermal bulk modulus equals pressure \(P\)), rather than infinite. A perfectly incompressible substance would have infinite bulk modulus, which is not true for gases.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Only the statements affirming that Young's modulus and shear modulus apply exclusively to solids and that bulk modulus is applicable across solids, liquids, and gases are correct. The final answer is 1 and 2 only.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक यह दर्शाते हैं कि कोई माध्यम विरूपक बलों के प्रति कैसी प्रतिक्रिया देता है। ठोसों का एक निश्चित आकार और निश्चित आयतन होता है, जिससे वे अनुदैर्ध्य प्रतिबल (यंग गुणांक \(Y\)) और अपरूपण प्रतिबल (अपरूपण गुणांक \(G\)) को सहन कर सकते हैं। तरल पदार्थ (द्रव और गैसें) अपरूपण दृढ़ता नहीं रखते हैं और स्थैतिक संतुलन में अपरूपण प्रतिबल को सहन नहीं कर सकते।

चरण 2: अनुदैर्ध्य और अपरूपण दृढ़ता का विश्लेषण
चूँकि तरलों का कोई निश्चित आकार नहीं होता है और वे स्थिर अवस्था में स्पर्शीय बलों का विरोध नहीं कर सकते, इसलिए यंग गुणांक और अपरूपण गुणांक केवल ठोस पदार्थों के लिए परिभाषित हैं। अतः यह कथन कि यंग गुणांक और अपरूपण गुणांक केवल ठोसों के लिए प्रासंगिक हैं, पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 3: विभिन्न अवस्थाओं में आयतन प्रत्यास्थता का विश्लेषण
पदार्थ की तीनों अवस्थाएं—ठोस, द्रव और गैस—समान द्रवस्थैतिक दाब लगाने पर आयतन परिवर्तन दर्शाती हैं। आयतन प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक \(B = -V \frac{\Delta P}{\Delta V}\) तीनों अवस्थाओं के लिए परिभाषित है, अतः यह कथन भी सत्य है।

चरण 4: गैसों की संपीड्यता का परीक्षण
गैसें अत्यधिक संपीड्य होती हैं और दाब बढ़ाने पर उनके आयतन में बहुत बड़ा परिवर्तन होता है। संपीड्यता \(k = \frac{1}{B}\) गैसों के लिए बहुत अधिक होती है, जिसका अर्थ है कि उनका आयतन गुणांक परिमित और अपेक्षाकृत कम होता है (समतापी आयतन गुणांक दाब \(P\) के बराबर होता है), न कि अनंत। अतः गैसों को असंपीड्य और अनंत आयतन गुणांक वाला बताना गलत है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल वे कथन सही हैं जो यह व्यक्त करते हैं कि यंग और अपरूपण गुणांक केवल ठोसों पर लागू होते हैं तथा आयतन गुणांक तीनों अवस्थाओं पर लागू होता है। सही उत्तर केवल 1 और 2 है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS11_CH08_STATEMENT3_Q02 - Critical points and behavior on the tensile stress-strain curve

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the features of a typical stress-strain curve for a metallic wire under tension:

  1. In the region from the origin to the proportional limit, stress is directly proportional to strain and Hooke's law is strictly obeyed.
  2. Beyond the elastic limit (yield point), unloading the wire does not restore its original length, resulting in a permanent set.
  3. A material is classified as brittle if its ultimate tensile strength point and fracture point are separated by a very large strain region.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

तनाव के अधीन एक धातु के तार के लिए विशिष्ट प्रतिबल-विकृति वक्र की विशेषताओं के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

  1. मूल बिंदु से आनुपातिक सीमा तक के क्षेत्र में, प्रतिबल विकृति के समानुपाती होता है और हुक के नियम का कड़ाई से पालन होता है।
  2. प्रत्यास्थता सीमा (पराभव बिंदु) से परे, तार से भार हटाने पर वह अपनी मूल लंबाई पुनः प्राप्त नहीं करता, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप एक स्थायी विरूपण (permanent set) रह जाता है।
  3. किसी पदार्थ को भंगुर के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है यदि उसका चरम तनन सामर्थ्य बिंदु और भंजन बिंदु एक बहुत बड़े विकृति क्षेत्र द्वारा अलग होते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The tensile stress-strain curve characterizes mechanical properties of a solid across distinct regimes: the linear proportional region, elastic region up to the yield point, plastic flow region, ultimate tensile strength, and fracture point.

Step 2: Proportional Region and Hooke's Law
From the origin to the proportional limit, the graph is a straight line. Here, stress is strictly linear with strain (\(\sigma = Y \varepsilon\)), fully obeying Hooke's law. Therefore, the assertion regarding the region up to the proportional limit is correct.

Step 3: Behavior Beyond the Yield Point
When the applied stress exceeds the elastic limit (yield point), the material enters the plastic deformation regime. Upon removing the deforming load, the strain does not trace back to zero; instead, a residual deformation known as a permanent set remains. Hence, the statement stating that a permanent set occurs beyond the elastic limit is correct.

Step 4: Classification of Ductile Versus Brittle Materials
Materials for which the plastic deformation zone between the ultimate tensile strength and the fracture point is large are ductile (they can be drawn into wires). Conversely, brittle materials fracture almost immediately after the elastic or ultimate limit without substantial plastic strain. Therefore, describing a material with a very large separation between ultimate tensile strength and fracture as brittle is scientifically incorrect; such a material is ductile.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct statements are those describing the adherence to Hooke's law up to the proportional limit and the retention of a permanent set beyond the elastic limit. The final answer is 1 and 2 only.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
तनन प्रतिबल-विकृति वक्र किसी ठोस के यांत्रिक गुणों को विभिन्न क्षेत्रों में प्रदर्शित करता है: आनुपातिक सीमा तक रैखिक क्षेत्र, पराभव बिंदु तक प्रत्यास्थ क्षेत्र, सुघट्य (प्लास्टिक) विरूपण क्षेत्र, चरम तनन सामर्थ्य और भंजन बिंदु।

चरण 2: आनुपातिक क्षेत्र और हुक का नियम
मूल बिंदु से आनुपातिक सीमा तक वक्र एक सीधी रेखा होता है। इस क्षेत्र में प्रतिबल, विकृति के सीधे समानुपाती होता है (\(\sigma = Y \varepsilon\)), और हुक के नियम का पूर्णतः पालन होता है। अतः आनुपातिक सीमा से संबंधित कथन सही है।

चरण 3: प्रत्यास्थता सीमा से परे व्यवहार
जब आरोपित प्रतिबल प्रत्यास्थ सीमा (पराभव बिंदु) से अधिक हो जाता है, तो पदार्थ प्लास्टिक क्षेत्र में प्रवेश कर जाता है। विरूपक बल हटाने पर विकृति शून्य पर वापस नहीं लौटती, बल्कि एक अवशिष्ट विरूपण (स्थायी विरूपण) रह जाता है। अतः यह कथन कि प्रत्यास्थ सीमा से परे स्थायी विरूपण रह जाता है, बिल्कुल सही है।

चरण 4: तन्य बनाम भंगुर पदार्थों का वर्गीकरण
वे पदार्थ जिनमें चरम तनन सामर्थ्य और भंजन बिंदु के बीच प्लास्टिक विरूपण का क्षेत्र बहुत बड़ा होता है, तन्य (ductile) कहलाते हैं। इसके विपरीत, भंगुर पदार्थों में चरम बिंदु के तुरंत बाद भंजन हो जाता है। अतः बड़े प्लास्टिक क्षेत्र वाले पदार्थ को भंगुर कहना गलत है; वह पदार्थ वास्तव में तन्य होता है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल वे कथन सही हैं जो आनुपातिक सीमा तक हुक के नियम के पालन और प्रत्यास्थ सीमा से परे स्थायी विरूपण की उपस्थिति को व्यक्त करते हैं। सही उत्तर केवल 1 और 2 है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS11_CH08_STATEMENT3_Q03 - Elastic potential energy density and work done during stretching

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the work done and elastic potential energy stored in a stretched wire:

  1. The total work done in stretching a wire of original length \(L\) by an elongation \(l\) is given by \(W = \frac{1}{2} F l\), where \(F\) is the final stretching force.
  2. The elastic potential energy stored per unit volume (energy density) of the wire equals \(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{stress} \times \text{strain}\).
  3. For two wires of identical length and cross-sectional area stretched by the same elongation, the wire made of rubber stores more elastic energy than the wire made of steel.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

खींचे गए तार में किए गए कार्य और संचित प्रत्यास्थ स्थितिज ऊर्जा के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

  1. मूल लंबाई \(L\) के एक तार को \(l\) लंबाई तक खींचने में किया गया कुल कार्य \(W = \frac{1}{2} F l\) द्वारा दिया जाता है, जहाँ \(F\) अंतिम खिंचाव बल है।
  2. तार के प्रति एकांक आयतन में संचित प्रत्यास्थ स्थितिज ऊर्जा (ऊर्जा घनत्व) \(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{प्रतिबल} \times \text{विकृति}\) के बराबर होती है।
  3. समान लंबाई और समान अनुप्रस्थ परिच्छेद क्षेत्रफल वाले दो तारों को समान विस्तार तक खींचने पर, रबर का तार स्टील के तार की तुलना में अधिक प्रत्यास्थ ऊर्जा संचित करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Relations and Principles
When a wire of length \(L\) and cross-sectional area \(A\) is stretched by a force that increases linearly from \(0\) to \(F\) producing an elongation \(l\), the instantaneous tension is \(f(x) = \frac{Y A}{L} x\).

Step 2: Derivation of Work Done
The work done by the stretching force is: \[ W = \int_0^l f(x) \, dx = \int_0^l \frac{Y A}{L} x \, dx = \frac{1}{2} \frac{Y A}{L} l^2 = \frac{1}{2} F l \] Thus, the statement identifying the work done as half the product of the final force and elongation is correct.

Step 3: Energy Stored per Unit Volume
The volume of the wire is \(V = A L\). Dividing total stored potential energy by volume yields: \[ u = \frac{W}{V} = \frac{\frac{1}{2} F l}{A L} = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{F}{A}\right) \left(\frac{l}{L}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{stress} \times \text{strain} \] In terms of Young's modulus, \(u = \frac{1}{2} Y (\text{strain})^2\). Thus, the assertion regarding the formula for energy density is completely valid.

Step 4: Energy Comparison for Identical Elongation
The stored elastic potential energy in terms of elongation \(l\) is: \[ W = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{Y A}{L}\right) l^2 \] Since the dimensions \(A\), \(L\), and the elongation \(l\) are identical for both wires, the stored energy is directly proportional to Young's modulus: \[ W \propto Y \] Because steel has a significantly higher Young's modulus than rubber (\(Y_{\text{steel}} \gg Y_{\text{rubber}}\)), the steel wire stores vastly more elastic potential energy than the rubber wire under the same elongation. Therefore, stating that rubber stores more energy than steel under equal elongation is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Only the statements stating that stretching work equals \(\frac{1}{2} F l\) and that elastic energy density equals \(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{stress} \times \text{strain}\) are correct. The final answer is 1 and 2 only.

चरण 1: दिए गए संबंध और सिद्धांत
जब लंबाई \(L\) और अनुप्रस्थ काट क्षेत्रफल \(A\) वाले तार को शून्य से \(F\) तक खिंचाव बल लगाकर \(l\) लंबाई तक खींचा जाता है, तो तात्कालिक खिंचाव बल \(f(x) = \frac{Y A}{L} x\) होता है।

चरण 2: किए गए कार्य की गणना
तार को खींचने में किया गया कुल कार्य समाकलन द्वारा प्राप्त होता है: \[ W = \int_0^l \frac{Y A}{L} x \, dx = \frac{1}{2} \frac{Y A}{L} l^2 = \frac{1}{2} F l \] अतः कुल कार्य को अंतिम बल और खिंचाव के गुणनफल का आधा बताने वाला कथन बिल्कुल सही है।

चरण 3: प्रति एकांक आयतन में संचित ऊर्जा (ऊर्जा घनत्व)
तार का कुल आयतन \(V = A L\) होता है। स्थितिज ऊर्जा को आयतन से विभाजित करने पर: \[ u = \frac{W}{V} = \frac{\frac{1}{2} F l}{A L} = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{F}{A}\right) \left(\frac{l}{L}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{प्रतिबल} \times \text{विकृति} \] अतः ऊर्जा घनत्व का सूत्र \(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{प्रतिबल} \times \text{विकृति}\) बताने वाला कथन पूर्णतः सत्य है।

चरण 4: समान खिंचाव के लिए ऊर्जा की तुलना
समान विस्तार \(l\) के लिए संचित प्रत्यास्थ ऊर्जा का सूत्र है: \[ W = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{Y A}{L}\right) l^2 \] चूँकि दोनों तारों के लिए \(A\), \(L\) और \(l\) समान हैं, इसलिए ऊर्जा सीधे यंग गुणांक के समानुपाती होती है: \[ W \propto Y \] चूँकि स्टील का यंग प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक रबर की तुलना में बहुत अधिक होता है (\(Y_{\text{steel}} \gg Y_{\text{rubber}}\)), अतः समान खिंचाव के लिए स्टील का तार रबर के तार की तुलना में कहीं अधिक ऊर्जा संचित करेगा। इसलिए रबर द्वारा अधिक ऊर्जा संचित करने का दावा गलत है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल वे कथन सही हैं जो किए गए कार्य को \(\frac{1}{2} F l\) और ऊर्जा घनत्व को \(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{प्रतिबल} \times \text{विकृति}\) के रूप में निरूपित करते हैं। सही उत्तर केवल 1 और 2 है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS11_CH08_STATEMENT3_Q04 - Structural design of beams and maximum height of mountains on Earth

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the practical applications of elastic behavior in structural engineering and geophysics:

  1. For a rectangular beam of length \(L\), breadth \(b\), and depth \(d\) supported at its ends and loaded at the center with load \(W\), the sag (depression) produced is \(\delta = \frac{W L^3}{4 b d^3 Y}\).
  2. To minimize bending depression while avoiding sideways buckling and unnecessary structural weight, steel girders are manufactured with an I-shaped cross section.
  3. The maximum height of mountains on Earth is limited to approximately \(10\text{ km}\) primarily because the hydrostatic pressure at the base exceeds the bulk modulus of the rock.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

संरचनात्मक इंजीनियरिंग और भूभौतिकी में प्रत्यास्थ व्यवहार के व्यावहारिक अनुप्रयोगों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

  1. लंबाई \(L\), चौड़ाई \(b\) और गहराई \(d\) वाले एक आयताकार धरन (बीम) के लिए, जो सिरों पर टिकी है और केंद्र पर \(W\) भार से लदी है, उत्पन्न अवनमन \(\delta = \frac{W L^3}{4 b d^3 Y}\) होता है।
  2. अनावश्यक संरचनात्मक भार को कम करने और पाशर्व बंकन (buckling) से बचते हुए अवनमन को न्यूनतम करने के लिए, स्टील गर्डर का निर्माण I-आकार के अनुप्रस्थ परिच्छेद के साथ किया जाता है।
  3. पृथ्वी पर पर्वतों की अधिकतम ऊंचाई लगभग \(10\text{ km}\) तक सीमित है क्योंकि आधार पर द्रवस्थैतिक दाब चट्टानों के आयतन प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक से अधिक हो जाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The structural deflection of loaded beams and the geophysical stability of geological mountains are governed by the elastic properties of materials, specifically bending rigidity under transverse load and plastic shear yield limit under gravitational base pressure.

Step 2: Depression of a Loaded Rectangular Beam
When a beam of length \(L\), breadth \(b\), and depth \(d\) supported at both ends carries a concentrated central weight \(W\), its vertical sag at the midpoint is derived from beam bending theory as: \[ \delta = \frac{W L^3}{4 b d^3 Y} \] Because the depression is inversely proportional to the cube of depth \(d^3\) and to the first power of breadth \(b\), increasing depth is much more effective than increasing breadth in minimizing depression. Therefore, the formula stated for beam sag is correct.

Step 3: Mechanics of I-Shaped Girders
Increasing depth \(d\) greatly reduces sag, but a tall, thin rectangular plate tends to bend sideways and buckle under load. Designing the beam with an I-shaped section provides a large depth with broad top and bottom flanges. This geometry provides high second moment of area, prevents lateral buckling, provides a large load-bearing surface, and significantly reduces structural weight. Thus, the statement describing the advantages of I-section girders is correct.

Step 4: Maximum Height of Mountains
At the base of a mountain of height \(h\) and rock density \(\rho\), the gravitational pressure is \(P = \rho g h\). Rock at the base experiences vertical pressure while surrounded by lateral rock. The material undergoes plastic flow (shear failure) when the shear stress exceeds the elastic shear limit (yielding strength), not because the hydrostatic pressure exceeds the bulk modulus. Rocks yield by shearing when \(\rho g h \approx 3 \times 10^8\text{ N/m}^2\), giving: \[ h_{\text{max}} \approx \frac{3 \times 10^8\text{ N/m}^2}{(3 \times 10^3\text{ kg/m}^3)(9.8\text{ m/s}^2)} \approx 10\text{ km} \] Because rock failure at the base is governed by shear yield strength rather than bulk modulus, the assertion attributing mountain height limit to bulk modulus is physically incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Only the statements correctly expressing beam depression as \(\frac{W L^3}{4 b d^3 Y}\) and elucidating the structural benefits of I-shaped girders are valid. The final answer is 1 and 2 only.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
भारित धरनों (बीम) का संरचनात्मक झुकाव और पर्वतों की भूभौतिकीय स्थिरता पदार्थों के प्रत्यास्थ गुणों, विशेष रूप से अनुप्रस्थ भार के तहत बंकन दृढ़ता और गुरुत्वीय आधार दाब के तहत अपरूपण पराभव सामर्थ्य द्वारा नियंत्रित होती है।

चरण 2: आयताकार धरन का अवनमन
जब लंबाई \(L\), चौड़ाई \(b\) और गहराई \(d\) वाली धरन दोनों सिरों पर टिकी हो और केंद्र पर भार \(W\) लगाया जाए, तो केंद्र पर उत्पन्न अवनमन का सूत्र है: \[ \delta = \frac{W L^3}{4 b d^3 Y} \] चूँकि अवनमन गहराई के घन \(d^3\) के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है, इसलिए गहराई बढ़ाना अवनमन कम करने के लिए सबसे प्रभावी होता है। अतः दिया गया अवनमन सूत्र पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 3: I-आकार के गर्डर की उपयोगिता
गहराई \(d\) बढ़ाने से अवनमन बहुत घट जाता है, लेकिन एक बहुत पतली और गहरी पट्टी भार के तहत तिरछी होकर मुड़ सकती है (buckling)। धरन को I-आकार का बनाने से गहरा अनुप्रस्थ परिच्छेद भी मिलता है और चौड़े सिरे इसे पार्श्व बंकन से बचाते हैं, साथ ही भार वहन करने हेतु पर्याप्त सतह मिलती है और अनावश्यक भार भी कम होता है। अतः I-आकार के गर्डर से संबंधित कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: पर्वतों की अधिकतम ऊंचाई की सीमा
ऊंचाई \(h\) और घनत्व \(\rho\) वाले पर्वत के आधार पर दाब \(P = \rho g h\) होता है। पर्वत के आधार पर उपस्थित चट्टानें तब बहने (प्लास्टिक विरूपण) लगती हैं जब अपरूपण प्रतिबल चट्टानों की अपरूपण प्रत्यास्थ सीमा (पराभव सामर्थ्य \(\approx 3 \times 10^8\text{ N/m}^2\)) को पार कर जाता है, न कि आयतन प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक के कारण। चूँकि यह सीमा अपरूपण सामर्थ्य द्वारा निर्धारित होती है, न कि आयतन गुणांक द्वारा, अतः पर्वत की ऊंचाई को आयतन गुणांक से सीमित बताना गलत है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल वे कथन सही हैं जो धरन के अवनमन सूत्र \(\frac{W L^3}{4 b d^3 Y}\) और I-आकार के गर्डर के लाभों को सही रूप में प्रस्तुत करते हैं। सही उत्तर केवल 1 और 2 है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MATCH_MCQ_Q01 - Matching elastic moduli with governing definitions

questiontext.text:
Match the elastic properties listed in List I with their corresponding physical definitions in List II:

List IList II
(A) Young's modulus(I) Ratio of hydraulic stress to volume strain
(B) Shear modulus(II) Ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain
(C) Bulk modulus(III) Ratio of tensile or compressive stress to longitudinal strain
(D) Poisson's ratio(IV) Ratio of shearing stress to shearing strain

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Modulus of elasticity is defined by Hooke's law as the ratio of stress to the corresponding strain for small deformations within the proportional limit. The specific modulus depends on the mode of deformation: longitudinal, shear, or volumetric. Lateral strain induced by longitudinal stress is described by Poisson's ratio.

Step 2: Analysis of Young's Modulus
Young's modulus \(Y\) measures the resistance of a solid body to elongation or compression parallel to the applied normal force. It is defined quantitatively as the ratio of tensile (or compressive) stress to longitudinal strain: \(Y = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon} = \frac{F / A}{\Delta L / L}\). Therefore, Young's modulus corresponds to the ratio of tensile or compressive stress to longitudinal strain.

Step 3: Analysis of Shear Modulus
Shear modulus \(G\) (also known as modulus of rigidity) describes the resistance of a body to shape change under tangential deforming forces applied parallel to opposite faces. It is defined as the ratio of tangential (shearing) stress to the resulting shearing strain: \(G = \frac{\sigma_s}{\theta} = \frac{F / A}{\Delta x / L}\). Therefore, shear modulus corresponds to the ratio of shearing stress to shearing strain.

Step 4: Analysis of Bulk Modulus and Poisson's Ratio
Bulk modulus \(B\) measures resistance to uniform volume compression under pressure and is defined as the ratio of hydraulic stress to the resulting volume strain: \(B = -\frac{p}{\Delta V / V}\). Poisson's ratio \(\nu\) describes the simultaneous transverse contraction accompanying longitudinal elongation within the elastic limit and is defined as the ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain: \(\nu = \frac{\Delta d / d}{\Delta L / L}\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Matching each term with its definition yields: Young's modulus pairs with ratio of tensile or compressive stress to longitudinal strain; Shear modulus pairs with ratio of shearing stress to shearing strain; Bulk modulus pairs with ratio of hydraulic stress to volume strain; and Poisson's ratio pairs with ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain. This establishes the combination: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MATCH_MCQ_Q02 - Matching stress strain curve key points

questiontext.text:
Match the key points and regions of a typical metal stress-strain curve in List I with their physical significance in List II:

List IList II
(A) Proportional limit(I) The point at which the material completely breaks or fractures under load
(B) Yield point(II) The maximum tensile stress that the material can sustain before necking occurs
(C) Ultimate tensile strength(III) The point up to which stress is directly proportional to strain and Hooke's law is obeyed
(D) Fracture point(IV) The elastic limit beyond which the material acquires permanent set and plastic deformation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In a standard tensile test of a metal, recording stress against strain produces a characteristic curve. This curve demarcates the proportional elastic region, the elastic limit, the plastic deformation domain, the peak load capacity, and the final failure point.

Step 2: Analysis of the Proportional Limit and Yield Point
The proportional limit represents the boundary of the strictly linear portion of the stress-strain curve from the origin. Up to this point, stress is directly proportional to strain, meaning Hooke's law is obeyed. The yield point (also called the elastic limit) is the point beyond which the material no longer returns to its original dimensions upon unloading; any deformation beyond this point produces a permanent set and plastic deformation.

Step 3: Analysis of Ultimate Tensile Strength and Fracture Point
The ultimate tensile strength is the maximum nominal stress that the material can sustain on the stress-strain curve. Beyond this peak point, localized necking develops and additional strain occurs even with decreasing applied load. The fracture point is the terminal point on the curve where structural separation occurs and the test specimen completely breaks.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Matching each feature with its physical description yields: Proportional limit pairs with the point up to which Hooke's law is obeyed; Yield point pairs with the elastic limit beyond which permanent set occurs; Ultimate tensile strength pairs with the maximum tensile stress sustained before necking; and Fracture point pairs with the point where the material breaks. This establishes the combination: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MATCH_MCQ_Q03 - Matching mechanical formulas with physical situations

questiontext.text:
Match the physical situations and phenomena in List I with their governing mathematical expressions in List II:

List IList II
(A) Depression of a rectangular beam loaded at the centre(I) \(u = \frac{1}{2} \times \sigma \times \varepsilon\)
(B) Elastic potential energy per unit volume of a stretched wire(II) \(\delta = \frac{W l^3}{4 b d^3 Y}\)
(C) Shearing strain of a rectangular block under tangential force(III) \(h_{\text{max}} = \frac{\sigma_{\text{limit}}}{\rho g}\)
(D) Maximum allowable height of a mountain on Earth(IV) \(\tan \theta = \frac{\Delta x}{L} \approx \theta\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The mechanical behaviour of solids under stress is governed by rigorous mathematical expressions derived from elastic moduli, equilibrium geometry, and energy conservation.

Step 2: Analysis of Beam Depression and Energy Density
For a horizontal rectangular beam of length \(l\), breadth \(b\), and depth \(d\) supported at its ends and loaded at the centre by a weight \(W\), the sag or depression is given by \(\delta = \frac{W l^3}{4 b d^3 Y}\), where \(Y\) is Young's modulus. For a wire under tensile stress \(\sigma\) and longitudinal strain \(\varepsilon\), the work done during elongation per unit volume is stored as elastic potential energy density \(u = \frac{1}{2} \times \sigma \times \varepsilon\).

Step 3: Analysis of Shearing Strain and Maximum Mountain Height
When a tangential force acts on a face of a cylinder or rectangular block of height \(L\), producing a relative horizontal displacement \(\Delta x\) between opposite faces, the shearing strain is defined as the angle of shear \(\tan \theta = \frac{\Delta x}{L} \approx \theta\). At the base of a mountain of height \(h\) and density \(\rho\), the unbalanced vertical weight creates a lateral shear stress approximately equal to \(h \rho g\). Setting this equal to the critical shear limit of rock \(\sigma_{\text{limit}}\) gives the maximum mountain height \(h_{\text{max}} = \frac{\sigma_{\text{limit}}}{\rho g}\).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Matching each situation with its mathematical expression yields: Depression of a rectangular beam pairs with \(\frac{W l^3}{4 b d^3 Y}\); Elastic potential energy density pairs with \(\frac{1}{2} \sigma \varepsilon\); Shearing strain pairs with \(\frac{\Delta x}{L} \approx \theta\); and Maximum mountain height pairs with \(\frac{\sigma_{\text{limit}}}{\rho g}\). This establishes the combination: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q01 - Tensile stress developed in uniform wire

questiontext.text: A tensile force of \(200\text{ N}\) is applied uniformly across the end of a metal wire having a cross-sectional area of \(2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2\). What is the tensile stress developed within the wire?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Applied tensile force: \(F = 200\text{ N}\).
Cross-sectional area: \(A = 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Tensile stress is defined as the internal restoring force per unit area normal to the cross-section. In static equilibrium, the restoring force equals the applied force: \(\sigma = \frac{F}{A}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\sigma = \frac{F}{A}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the formula:
\(\sigma = \frac{200\text{ N}}{2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2} = 100 \times 10^6\text{ N m}^{-2} = 1.0 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are \(\text{N m}^{-2}\) (Pascals), and the magnitude is physically appropriate for elastic tensile stress in metals. Therefore, the tensile stress developed in the wire is \(1.0 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q02 - Longitudinal strain in stretched steel wire

questiontext.text: A metal wire of initial length \(2.0\text{ m}\) is stretched along its length such that its elongation is \(1.0\text{ mm}\). The longitudinal strain produced in the wire is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial length of the wire: \(L = 2.0\text{ m}\).
Change in length: \(\Delta L = 1.0\text{ mm} = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Longitudinal strain is defined as the ratio of change in length to the original length.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\varepsilon = \frac{\Delta L}{L}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:
\(\varepsilon = \frac{1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}}{2.0\text{ m}} = 0.5 \times 10^{-3} = 5.0 \times 10^{-4}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Strain is a dimensionless quantity. In percentage form, this corresponds to \(0.05\%\), which is well within normal elastic limits. Therefore, the longitudinal strain is \(5.0 \times 10^{-4}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q03 - Shearing strain produced in sheared block

questiontext.text: A solid metal block of height \(0.50\text{ m}\) has its bottom face fixed to a horizontal surface. When a horizontal force is applied to its upper face, the upper face undergoes a relative displacement of \(0.25\text{ mm}\). The shearing strain produced in the block is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Height of the block: \(L = 0.50\text{ m}\).
Relative lateral displacement of the top face: \(\Delta x = 0.25\text{ mm} = 2.5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Shearing strain is defined as the ratio of relative displacement between opposite parallel faces to the perpendicular distance separating them: \(\text{Shearing strain} = \frac{\Delta x}{L} = \tan \theta \approx \theta\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\theta \approx \frac{\Delta x}{L}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the numerical values:
\(\theta = \frac{2.5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}}{0.50\text{ m}} = 5.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ rad}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The shearing angle \(\theta\) is dimensionless (radians) and small (\(\ll 1\text{ rad}\)), verifying that the linear approximation \(\tan \theta \approx \theta\) is exact. Therefore, the shearing strain is \(5.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ rad}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q04 - Volume strain of submerged solid sphere

questiontext.text: A solid sphere of initial volume \(0.50\text{ m}^3\) is submerged in a deep fluid where uniform hydraulic pressure causes its volume to decrease by \(1.5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^3\). The volume strain experienced by the sphere is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial volume of the sphere: \(V = 0.50\text{ m}^3\).
Change in volume: \(|\Delta V| = 1.5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^3\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Volume strain is defined as the absolute ratio of change in volume to the original volume: \(\text{Volume strain} = \frac{|\Delta V|}{V}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\text{Volume strain} = \frac{|\Delta V|}{V}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the ratio:
\(\text{Volume strain} = \frac{1.5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^3}{0.50\text{ m}^3} = 3.0 \times 10^{-4}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Volume strain is dimensionless and non-negative. Therefore, the volume strain experienced by the sphere is \(3.0 \times 10^{-4}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q05 - Compressibility of solid copper from bulk modulus

questiontext.text: Given that the bulk modulus of copper is \(140\text{ GPa}\) (\(140 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}\)), what is the compressibility of copper?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Bulk modulus of copper: \(B = 140\text{ GPa} = 140 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2} = 1.40 \times 10^{11}\text{ Pa}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Compressibility \(k\) is defined as the reciprocal of the bulk modulus: \(k = \frac{1}{B}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(k = \frac{1}{B}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \(B = 1.40 \times 10^{11}\text{ Pa}\):
\(k = \frac{1}{1.40 \times 10^{11}\text{ Pa}} = \frac{1}{1.40} \times 10^{-11}\text{ Pa}^{-1} \approx 0.7143 \times 10^{-11}\text{ Pa}^{-1} = 7.14 \times 10^{-12}\text{ Pa}^{-1}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The unit of compressibility is \(\text{Pa}^{-1}\) or \(\text{m}^2 \text{N}^{-1}\), which is the inverse of pressure. Therefore, the compressibility of copper is \(7.14 \times 10^{-12}\text{ Pa}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q06 - Tensile stress in stretched structural steel rod

questiontext.text: A structural steel rod has a circular cross-section with radius \(10\text{ mm}\) and length \(1.0\text{ m}\). An axial tensile force of \(100\text{ kN}\) stretches it along its length. Taking \(\pi \approx 3.14\), the tensile stress developed in the rod is closest to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of the rod: \(r = 10\text{ mm} = 1.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m}\).
Applied axial force: \(F = 100\text{ kN} = 1.0 \times 10^5\text{ N}\).
Length: \(L = 1.0\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Tensile stress is defined as the normal tensile force per unit cross-sectional area: \(\sigma = \frac{F}{A}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Area of circular cross-section: \(A = \pi r^2\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the cross-sectional area:
\(A = 3.14 \times (1.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m})^2 = 3.14 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2\).
Compute the tensile stress:
\(\sigma = \frac{1.0 \times 10^5\text{ N}}{3.14 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2} \approx 3.1847 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The computed value rounded to three significant figures is \(3.18 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}\). Therefore, the tensile stress developed in the rod is \(3.18 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q07 - Elongation produced in stretched steel rod

questiontext.text: A structural steel rod of length \(1.0\text{ m}\) is subjected to an axial tensile stress of \(3.18 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}\). If the Young's modulus of structural steel is \(2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}\), the elongation of the rod is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial length: \(L = 1.0\text{ m}\).
Tensile stress: \(\sigma = 3.18 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}\).
Young's modulus: \(Y = 2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Hooke's law relates stress to longitudinal strain: \(\sigma = Y \varepsilon = Y \frac{\Delta L}{L}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\Delta L = \frac{\sigma L}{Y}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given quantities:
\(\Delta L = \frac{(3.18 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2})(1.0\text{ m})}{2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}} = 1.59 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 1.59\text{ mm}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The strain is \(\frac{1.59 \times 10^{-3}}{1.0} = 0.159\%\), which lies comfortably within the elastic proportional region for steel. Therefore, the elongation of the rod is \(1.59\text{ mm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q08 - Fractional compression of ocean water at depth

questiontext.text: At a depth of \(3000\text{ m}\) in the ocean, calculate the percentage compression \(\left(\frac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100\%\right)\) of water, given that the density of water is \(1000\text{ kg m}^{-3}\), \(g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}\), and the bulk modulus of water is \(2.2 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Depth: \(h = 3000\text{ m}\).
Density of water: \(\rho = 1000\text{ kg m}^{-3}\).
Gravitational acceleration: \(g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}\).
Bulk modulus of water: \(B = 2.2 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Hydrostatic gauge pressure provides the hydraulic stress: \(p = h \rho g\). Bulk modulus relates pressure to fractional volume change: \(B = \frac{p}{\Delta V / V}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\frac{\Delta V}{V} = \frac{p}{B} = \frac{h \rho g}{B}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate gauge pressure:
\(p = 3000\text{ m} \times 1000\text{ kg m}^{-3} \times 10\text{ m s}^{-2} = 3.0 \times 10^7\text{ N m}^{-2}\).
Compute fractional compression:
\(\frac{\Delta V}{V} = \frac{3.0 \times 10^7\text{ N m}^{-2}}{2.2 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}} = \frac{3}{220} \approx 0.013636\).
Expressed as a percentage:
\(0.013636 \times 100\% \approx 1.36\%\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Water is nearly incompressible, so a small value of \(\approx 1.36\%\) at 3 km depth is physically sound. Therefore, the percentage compression is \(1.36\%\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q09 - Maximum height of mountain based on shear limit

questiontext.text: A mountain of rock has uniform density \(\rho = 3.0 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}\). If the critical shearing stress at which the base rocks begin to flow is \(3.0 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}\) and \(g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}\), the maximum theoretical height of the mountain on Earth is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Rock density: \(\rho = 3.0 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}\).
Critical shear stress: \(\sigma_{\text{shear}} = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}\).
Gravitational acceleration: \(g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The vertical load per unit area at the base of height \(h\) is \(h \rho g\). Because the mountain sides are unconstrained, this gives rise to an unconfined shear stress of magnitude approximately \(h \rho g\). For stability, \(h \rho g \le \sigma_{\text{shear}}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(h_{\max} = \frac{\sigma_{\text{shear}}}{\rho g}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the parameters:
\(h_{\max} = \frac{3.0 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}}{(3.0 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3})(10\text{ m s}^{-2})} = \frac{3.0 \times 10^8}{3.0 \times 10^4} = 10^4\text{ m} = 10\text{ km}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated height of \(10\text{ km}\) exceeds the height of Mount Everest (\(\approx 8.85\text{ km}\)), providing a consistent physical upper bound. Therefore, the maximum theoretical height is \(10\text{ km}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q10 - Ratio of Young moduli for steel and copper

questiontext.text: A steel wire of length \(4.7\text{ m}\) and cross-sectional area \(3.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}^2\) stretches by the same amount as a copper wire of length \(3.5\text{ m}\) and cross-sectional area \(4.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}^2\) under the same applied load. What is the ratio of the Young's modulus of steel to that of copper \(\left(\frac{Y_s}{Y_c}\right)\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Steel wire: \(L_s = 4.7\text{ m}\), \(A_s = 3.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}^2\).
Copper wire: \(L_c = 3.5\text{ m}\), \(A_c = 4.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}^2\).
Both experience equal force \(F\) and equal extension \(\Delta L\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Young's modulus is given by \(Y = \frac{F L}{A \Delta L}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\frac{Y_s}{Y_c} = \left(\frac{L_s}{L_c}\right) \times \left(\frac{A_c}{A_s}\right)\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:
\(\frac{Y_s}{Y_c} = \left(\frac{4.7}{3.5}\right) \times \left(\frac{4.0 \times 10^{-5}}{3.0 \times 10^{-5}}\right) = \frac{4.7 \times 4.0}{3.5 \times 3.0} = \frac{18.8}{10.5} \approx 1.7905\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio \(\approx 1.79\) matches standard values (\(Y_{\text{steel}} / Y_{\text{copper}} \approx 200 / 110 = 1.82\)). Therefore, the ratio of Young's modulus of steel to that of copper is \(1.79\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q11 - Minimum cross sectional area of crane steel rope

questiontext.text: A crane is designed to lift a maximum mass of \(10\text{ metric tonnes}\) (\(1\text{ metric tonne} = 1000\text{ kg}\)). To prevent permanent deformation, the tensile stress developed in its steel rope must not exceed the yield strength \(\sigma_y = 300 \times 10^6\text{ N m}^{-2}\). Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\), the minimum required cross-sectional area of the rope is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass to lift: \(M = 10 \times 1000\text{ kg} = 1.0 \times 10^4\text{ kg}\).
Yield strength: \(\sigma_y = 300 \times 10^6\text{ N m}^{-2}\).
Acceleration of gravity: \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
To prevent permanent plastic extension, working stress \(\sigma = \frac{M g}{A} \le \sigma_y\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(A_{\min} = \frac{M g}{\sigma_y}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate total weight:
\(W = 1.0 \times 10^4\text{ kg} \times 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2} = 9.8 \times 10^4\text{ N}\).
Compute minimum cross-sectional area:
\(A_{\min} = \frac{9.8 \times 10^4\text{ N}}{300 \times 10^6\text{ N m}^{-2}} = \frac{9.8}{3} \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2 \approx 3.267 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Rounding to three significant figures yields \(3.27 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2\). Therefore, the minimum cross-sectional area required is \(3.27 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q12 - Fractional volume change of glass slab under pressure

questiontext.text: A glass slab is subjected to a uniform hydraulic pressure of \(10.0\text{ atm}\). Given that \(1\text{ atm} = 1.013 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}\) and the bulk modulus of glass is \(37.0 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}\), the fractional change in volume \(\left|\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right|\) of the glass slab is closest to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Pressure: \(p = 10.0\text{ atm} = 10.0 \times 1.013 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} = 1.013 \times 10^6\text{ N m}^{-2}\).
Bulk modulus of glass: \(B = 37.0 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Bulk modulus relates hydraulic pressure to fractional volume change: \(B = \frac{p}{|\Delta V / V|}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\left|\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right| = \frac{p}{B}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the parameters:
\(\left|\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right| = \frac{1.013 \times 10^6\text{ N m}^{-2}}{37.0 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}} = \frac{1.013}{37.0} \times 10^{-3} \approx 0.027378 \times 10^{-3} = 2.74 \times 10^{-5}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The fractional volume change is dimensionless and very small (\(\sim 10^{-5}\)), consistent with glass under 10 atm. Therefore, the fractional change in volume is \(2.74 \times 10^{-5}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q13 - Elastic potential energy density in stretched wire

questiontext.text: A metal wire is put under a tensile stress of \(4.0 \times 10^7\text{ N m}^{-2}\), producing a longitudinal strain of \(2.0 \times 10^{-4}\). The elastic potential energy stored per unit volume in the wire is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Tensile stress: \(\sigma = 4.0 \times 10^7\text{ N m}^{-2}\).
Longitudinal strain: \(\varepsilon = 2.0 \times 10^{-4}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Within the elastic limit, elastic potential energy per unit volume \(u\) is given by half the product of stress and strain.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(u = \frac{1}{2} \sigma \varepsilon\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:
\(u = \frac{1}{2} \times (4.0 \times 10^7\text{ N m}^{-2}) \times (2.0 \times 10^{-4}) = 4.0 \times 10^3\text{ J m}^{-3}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units check: \(\text{N m}^{-2} = \text{J m}^{-3}\). The factor of \(\frac{1}{2}\) accounts for the linear increase of restoring force with extension. Therefore, the elastic energy stored per unit volume is \(4.0 \times 10^3\text{ J m}^{-3}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q14 - Total work done in stretching steel wire

questiontext.text: A steel wire of original length \(2.0\text{ m}\) and cross-sectional area \(1.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2\) is stretched by an elongation of \(2.0\text{ mm}\). If the Young's modulus of steel is \(2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}\), the total work done in stretching the wire is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length: \(L = 2.0\text{ m}\).
Area: \(A = 1.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2\).
Elongation: \(l = 2.0\text{ mm} = 2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}\).
Young's modulus: \(Y = 2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Work done in stretching a wire within its elastic limit is stored as elastic potential energy: \(W = \frac{1}{2} \frac{Y A l^2}{L}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(W = \frac{Y A l^2}{2 L}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given numerical values:
\(W = \frac{(2.0 \times 10^{11})(1.0 \times 10^{-6})(2.0 \times 10^{-3})^2}{2 \times 2.0} = \frac{(2.0 \times 10^5)(4.0 \times 10^{-6})}{4.0} = \frac{0.80}{4.0} = 0.20\text{ J}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The work done is positive and in Joules. Therefore, the total work done in stretching the wire is \(0.20\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q15 - Maximum load supported by ski chairlift cable

questiontext.text: A steel cable with circular cross-section of radius \(1.5\text{ cm}\) supports a chairlift at a ski resort. If the maximum permissible tensile stress in the cable is \(1.0 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}\), what is the maximum load the cable can support? (Take \(\pi \approx 3.14\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of the cable: \(r = 1.5\text{ cm} = 1.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m}\).
Maximum permissible stress: \(\sigma_{\max} = 1.0 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Maximum load supported is the product of maximum permissible stress and cross-sectional area: \(F_{\max} = \sigma_{\max} A\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(A = \pi r^2\) and \(F_{\max} = \sigma_{\max} \pi r^2\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate cross-sectional area:
\(A = 3.1416 \times (1.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m})^2 = 3.1416 \times 2.25 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2 \approx 7.0686 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2\).
Compute maximum load:
\(F_{\max} = (1.0 \times 10^8\text{ N m}^{-2}) \times (7.0686 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2) \approx 7.07 \times 10^4\text{ N}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
This load corresponds to supporting a mass of roughly \(\frac{7.07 \times 10^4}{9.8} \approx 7200\text{ kg}\), typical for a ski chairlift span. Therefore, the maximum load the cable can support is \(7.07 \times 10^4\text{ N}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q16 - Young modulus calculated from stress strain curve

questiontext.text: In a standard tensile test of a metal specimen, the linear proportional region of the stress-strain curve shows that an applied stress of \(150 \times 10^6\text{ N m}^{-2}\) corresponds to a strain of \(0.002\). What is the Young's modulus of this material?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Stress: \(\sigma = 150 \times 10^6\text{ N m}^{-2}\).
Strain: \(\varepsilon = 0.002 = 2.0 \times 10^{-3}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
In the linear proportional region, Hooke's law holds: Young's modulus is the slope of the stress-strain curve: \(Y = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(Y = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the ratio:
\(Y = \frac{150 \times 10^6\text{ N m}^{-2}}{2.0 \times 10^{-3}} = 75 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2} = 7.5 \times 10^{10}\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The modulus \(75\text{ GPa}\) is characteristic of structural aluminium alloys (\(\sim 70\text{ GPa}\)). Therefore, the Young's modulus of the material is \(7.5 \times 10^{10}\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q17 - Lateral contraction of stretched steel wire

questiontext.text: A steel wire of original diameter \(2.0\text{ mm}\) undergoes a longitudinal strain of \(1.0 \times 10^{-3}\) under tension. If the Poisson's ratio for the steel is \(0.30\), what is the contraction in the diameter of the wire?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Original diameter: \(d = 2.0 ext{ mm}\).
Longitudinal strain: \(\varepsilon_{ ext{long}} = 1.0 imes 10^{-3}\).
Poisson's ratio: \( u = 0.30\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Poisson's ratio relates lateral strain to longitudinal strain: \( u = rac{\varepsilon_{ ext{lateral}}}{\varepsilon_{ ext{long}}} = rac{\Delta d / d}{\Delta L / L}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\Delta d = u \cdot d \cdot \varepsilon_{ ext{long}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:
\(\Delta d = 0.30 imes (2.0 ext{ mm}) imes (1.0 imes 10^{-3}) = 6.0 imes 10^{-4} ext{ mm}\) (or \(0.60\ \mu ext{m}\)).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The diameter decreases under tension, and the magnitude (\(0.6\ \mu ext{m}\)) is typical for elastic lateral contraction. Therefore, the contraction in diameter is \(6.0 imes 10^{-4} ext{ mm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q18 - Load required to stretch connected series wires

questiontext.text: A copper wire of length \(2.2\text{ m}\) and a steel wire of length \(1.6\text{ m}\), each of diameter \(3.0\text{ mm}\), are joined end-to-end and stretched by an applied load \(W\). If the total elongation produced in the composite wire is \(0.70\text{ mm}\), \(Y_{\text{copper}} = 1.1 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}\), and \(Y_{\text{steel}} = 2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}\), the magnitude of the load \(W\) is closest to: (Take \(\pi \approx 3.14\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Lengths: \(L_c = 2.2\text{ m}\), \(L_s = 1.6\text{ m}\).
Common diameter: \(d = 3.0\text{ mm} \implies r = 1.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}\).
Net elongation: \(\Delta L = \Delta L_c + \Delta L_s = 0.70\text{ mm} = 7.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}\).
Moduli: \(Y_c = 1.1 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}\), \(Y_s = 2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Joined in series, both wires experience the same tension \(W\) and share identical cross-sectional area \(A = \pi r^2\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\Delta L_c = \frac{W L_c}{A Y_c}\), \(\Delta L_s = \frac{W L_s}{A Y_s}\), giving \(\frac{\Delta L_c}{\Delta L_s} = \left(\frac{Y_s}{Y_c}\right) \left(\frac{L_c}{L_s}\right)\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the elongation ratio:
\(\frac{\Delta L_c}{\Delta L_s} = \left(\frac{2.0 \times 10^{11}}{1.1 \times 10^{11}}\right) \times \left(\frac{2.2}{1.6}\right) = \frac{20}{11} \times 1.375 = 2.5\).
Thus \(\Delta L_c = 2.5 \Delta L_s\). With \(\Delta L_c + \Delta L_s = 7.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}\):
\(3.5 \Delta L_s = 7.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m} \implies \Delta L_s = 2.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}\), and \(\Delta L_c = 5.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}\).
Compute cross-sectional area:
\(A = \pi (1.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m})^2 = 3.1416 \times 2.25 \times 10^{-6} \approx 7.0686 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2\).
Calculate load \(W\):
\(W = \frac{A Y_c \Delta L_c}{L_c} = \frac{(7.0686 \times 10^{-6})(1.1 \times 10^{11})(5.0 \times 10^{-4})}{2.2} = \frac{0.38877}{2.2} \approx 176.7\text{ N} \approx 1.8 \times 10^2\text{ N}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Cross-checking with steel elongation yields the exact same value \(W \approx 177\text{ N}\). Therefore, the applied load is \(1.8 \times 10^2\text{ N}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q19 - Elongation of loaded brass wire in series

questiontext.text: A steel wire of unloaded length \(1.5\text{ m}\) hangs vertically from a ceiling supporting a \(4.0\text{ kg}\) mass. From this \(4.0\text{ kg}\) mass, a brass wire of unloaded length \(1.0\text{ m}\) hangs vertically supporting a \(6.0\text{ kg}\) mass. Both wires have a diameter of \(0.25\text{ cm}\). If \(Y_{\text{brass}} = 0.91 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}\) and \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\), the elongation of the brass wire is closest to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Diameter of brass wire: \(d = 0.25\text{ cm} = 2.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} \implies r = 1.25 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}\).
Length: \(L_b = 1.0\text{ m}\).
Mass suspended directly below brass wire: \(m_2 = 6.0\text{ kg}\).
Young's modulus of brass: \(Y_b = 0.91 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}\), and \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The brass wire supports only the lower mass of \(6.0\text{ kg}\), so the tension in the brass wire is \(F_b = m_2 g\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\Delta L_b = \frac{F_b L_b}{A Y_b}\) where \(A = \pi r^2\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Compute cross-sectional area:
\(A = \pi (1.25 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m})^2 = 3.1416 \times 1.5625 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2 \approx 4.9087 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2\).
Compute tension in the brass wire:
\(F_b = 6.0\text{ kg} \times 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2} = 58.8\text{ N}\).
Compute elongation:
\(\Delta L_b = \frac{58.8\text{ N} \times 1.0\text{ m}}{(4.9087 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2)(0.91 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2})} = \frac{58.8}{4.4669 \times 10^5} \approx 1.316 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The upper 4 kg mass does not act on the brass wire; only the bottom 6 kg mass stretches it. Rounding gives \(1.32 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}\). Therefore, the elongation of the brass wire is \(1.32 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q20 - Compression of thighbones in human circus pyramid

questiontext.text: In a circus pyramid act, the legs of a performer lying on his back support a balanced mass of \(280\text{ kg}\). The mass of the performer himself is \(60\text{ kg}\). Each of his two thighbones (femurs) has an effective length of \(50\text{ cm}\) and radius \(2.0\text{ cm}\). If Young's modulus of bone is \(9.4 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}\) and \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\), determine the amount by which each thighbone gets compressed under the extra load:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Total mass of pyramid: \(280\text{ kg}\); mass of performer: \(60\text{ kg}\).
Length of femur: \(L = 50\text{ cm} = 0.50\text{ m}\); radius: \(r = 2.0\text{ cm} = 0.020\text{ m}\).
Modulus of bone: \(Y = 9.4 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}\); \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The extra mass supported by the performer's legs is \(M_{\text{ext}} = 280 - 60 = 220\text{ kg}\). This weight is shared equally between the two thighbones.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Force on each bone: \(F = \frac{M_{\text{ext}} g}{2}\).
Compression: \(\Delta L = \frac{F L}{A Y}\) where \(A = \pi r^2\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate force on each thighbone:
\(F = \frac{220 \times 9.8}{2} = 1078\text{ N}\).
Compute cross-sectional area:
\(A = \pi (0.020\text{ m})^2 = 3.1416 \times 4.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2 \approx 1.2566 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^2\).
Calculate compression:
\(\Delta L = \frac{1078 \times 0.50}{(1.2566 \times 10^{-3})(9.4 \times 10^9)} = \frac{539}{1.1812 \times 10^7} \approx 4.563 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m} = 4.55 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The compression is very small (\(\approx 0.045\text{ mm}\)), which is expected for strong human skeletal bone under dynamic balance. Therefore, the compression of each thighbone is \(4.55 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q21 - Vertical shear deflection of fixed aluminium cube

questiontext.text: An aluminium cube of edge length \(10\text{ cm}\) has one face firmly fixed to a vertical wall. A mass of \(100\text{ kg}\) is attached to the opposite vertical face. Given that the shear modulus of aluminium is \(25\text{ GPa}\) (\(25 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}\)) and \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\), the vertical deflection of this face is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Edge length of cube: \(L = 10\text{ cm} = 0.10\text{ m}\).
Area of the face: \(A = L^2 = (0.10\text{ m})^2 = 0.010\text{ m}^2\).
Mass attached: \(m = 100\text{ kg}\); \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\).
Shear modulus: \(G = 25 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
The downward tangential shear force is \(F = m g\). Shear modulus relates shear stress to shear strain: \(G = \frac{F / A}{\Delta y / L}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\Delta y = \frac{F L}{A G}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the shear force:
\(F = 100\text{ kg} \times 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2} = 980\text{ N}\).
Calculate the vertical deflection:
\(\Delta y = \frac{980\text{ N} \times 0.10\text{ m}}{(0.010\text{ m}^2)(25 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2})} = \frac{98}{2.5 \times 10^8} = 3.92 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The shear deflection is of the order of sub-microns, well within the linear shear elasticity regime for metals. Therefore, the vertical deflection of the face is \(3.92 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q22 - Elongation of wire whirling in vertical circle

questiontext.text: A mass of \(14.5\text{ kg}\) is attached to the end of a steel wire of unstretched length \(1.0\text{ m}\) and cross-sectional area \(0.065\text{ cm}^2\). The mass is whirled in a vertical circle with an angular velocity of \(2\text{ rev s}^{-1}\) at the bottom of the circle. If \(Y_{\text{steel}} = 2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}\) and \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\), the elongation of the wire at the lowest point is closest to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass: \(m = 14.5\text{ kg}\).
Unstretched length: \(L = 1.0\text{ m}\).
Rotational frequency: \(\nu = 2\text{ rev s}^{-1} \implies \omega = 2\pi \nu = 4\pi\text{ rad s}^{-1} \approx 12.566\text{ rad s}^{-1}\).
Cross-sectional area: \(A = 0.065\text{ cm}^2 = 6.5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2\).
Young's modulus: \(Y = 2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}\); \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
At the lowest point of the vertical circle, the tension in the wire must provide the centripetal acceleration and support the gravitational weight: \(T = m g + m \omega^2 L\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\Delta L = \frac{T L}{A Y}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the centripetal force:
\(m \omega^2 L = 14.5 \times (4\pi)^2 \times 1.0 = 14.5 \times 16 \pi^2 = 232 \pi^2 \approx 232 \times 9.8696 \approx 2289.7\text{ N}\).
Calculate the weight:
\(m g = 14.5 \times 9.8 = 142.1\text{ N}\).
Total tension at the lowest point:
\(T = 2289.7 + 142.1 = 2431.8\text{ N}\).
Calculate elongation:
\(\Delta L = \frac{2431.8 \times 1.0}{(6.5 \times 10^{-6})(2.0 \times 10^{11})} = \frac{2431.8}{1.30 \times 10^6} \approx 1.8706 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 1.87\text{ mm}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The elongation is \(1.87\text{ mm}\), which is less than 0.2% of the unstretched length, confirming that the radius approximation is consistent and accurate. Therefore, the elongation of the wire at the lowest point is \(1.87 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MECHANICAL_PROPERTIES_OF_SOLIDS_MCQ_Q23 - Density of ocean water under high depth pressure

questiontext.text: At the surface of the ocean, the density of water is \(\rho_0 = 1.03 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}\). At a certain depth, the gauge pressure is \(80.0\text{ atm}\). Given that \(1\text{ atm} = 1.013 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}\) and the bulk modulus of water is \(B = 2.2 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}\), the density of water at this depth is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Surface density: \(\rho_0 = 1.03 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}\).
Pressure: \(p = 80.0\text{ atm} = 80.0 \times 1.013 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} = 8.104 \times 10^6\text{ N m}^{-2}\).
Bulk modulus of water: \(B = 2.2 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
